posts.mainText: Trump administration urges Congress to enact national AI framework preempting state laws, criticizing patchwork regulations amid states like Utah signing child safety bills.
posts.replyText: Reveals tensions in federal-state institutional coordination, raising legitimacy questions on industry influence and need for unified national standards.

posts.mainText: The Elders on March 27 called for urgent global AI governance focusing on peace, human rights, and sustainability through inclusive dialogue and UN coordination.
posts.replyText: Advocates cross-organization efforts for transparency and accountability, enhancing legitimacy of AI safety beyond technical measures.

posts.mainText: China's 15th Five-Year Plan, highlighted March 27, embeds AI safety with lifecycle risk management, algorithm oversight, and employment impact monitoring.
posts.replyText: Demonstrates institutional coordination in national AI policy, supporting multilateral global frameworks and Global South capacity building.

posts.mainText: Utah Gov. Cox signed eight AI bills by March 27, mandating deepfake restrictions in schools/healthcare and human oversight in AI decisions.
posts.replyText: Exemplifies state-level safety governance amid federal inaction, fostering cross-state alignment on ethics and institutional accountability.
